title: Extraction and Border
premise: Ada Whitlock, a whistle-blower living under four names, has spent six years laundering inconvenient truths through cases no one will claim — until a stranger named Elias Vance repays a favor she has no memory of doing, and drags her into a conspiracy inside the border-security agency she once exposed. The secret at its center is a kill-list algorithm buried in a deportation pipeline, and both a corrupt deputy director and the federal agent hunting Ada want it. To survive, Ada must decide whether to trade the one secret worth killing for — her own unredacted identity — and in the end she chooses to burn all four names at once, testifying publicly and vanishing into a fifth name she finally chooses for herself, while Elias takes the fall that keeps her free.
about_author: J. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former policy analyst who spent four years inside government contracting offices before leaving to write full-time. They live near a border town they refuse to name, and write only at night.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ada Whitlock, working under the name Mara Voss at a document-archive job, receives a package containing records of a favor done for her in 2019 — one she never performed. POV: Ada. The emotional beat is unease: someone knows a version of her that doesn't exist, and the interest on that phantom debt is already accruing.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Woman
chapters.summary: A tour of Ada's tradecraft: her rotation schedule, dead-drop habits, and the rules that keep her alive. POV: Ada. The beat is controlled loneliness — she is safe because she is no one, and the chapter quietly shows the cost of that.

chapters.title: Elias Vance, Returning
chapters.summary: The stranger from the package appears at Ada's workplace: Elias Vance, a former border-agency data contractor, claims she saved his life years ago and now owes her the truth. POV: Elias. The beat is magnetic ambiguity — we don't know if he's a savior or a lure.

chapters.title: The Pipeline
chapters.summary: Elias shows Ada fragments of an algorithm embedded in the deportation system — one that flags people for disappearance, not removal. POV: Elias. The beat is dread crystallizing into purpose as Ada recognizes the architecture of her own old whistle-blow.

chapters.title: Deputy Director Cole
chapters.summary: Introduce Raymond Cole, the deputy director whose career the algorithm protects, as he learns a ghost from 2019 may still be alive. POV: Cole. The beat is cold, patient menace — corruption presented as competent management.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ada tests Elias's story and finds it half-true: he was saved, but not by her — by the woman whose identity Ada stole. POV: Ada. The beat is guilt surfacing; belonging to a dead woman's name is its own debt.

chapters.title: The Agent at the Door
chapters.summary: Federal agent Priya Raman, hunting the 2019 leak for six years, interviews Ada's current alias. POV: Priya. The beat is cat-and-mouse civility — two careful women, each certain she's the smarter one.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Ada and Elias copy a fragment of the kill-list from a contractor server; the extraction triggers a silent alarm Cole planted. POV: Elias. The beat is adrenaline and the first irrevocable step — they're inside it now.

chapters.title: What Cole Knows
chapters.summary: Cole identifies Mara Voss as a probable alias and chooses surveillance over arrest, wanting the full network before he moves. POV: Cole. The beat is tightening vise — Ada's four names are becoming a map of her.

chapters.title: The Woman I Stole From
chapters.summary: Ada confesses to Elias that her first alias belonged to Dana Reyes, a colleague who died in a staged accident after the 2019 leak. POV: Ada. The beat is raw grief converted into resolve: this is no longer survival, it's atonement.

chapters.title: Raman's Second Theory
chapters.summary: Priya realizes the 2019 leaker and the current intrusion share a signature — and starts building her own file on Cole, not the ghost. POV: Priya. The beat is the hunter's crisis of loyalty: truth or career.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Holed up after the alarm, Ada and Elias plan the full extraction; intimacy grows alongside the body count of their options. POV: Elias. The beat is fragile trust — two people who lie professionally choosing honesty with each other.

chapters.title: The List Has a Face
chapters.summary: They decode the first name on the kill-list: a teenage asylum seeker already flagged for 'expedited processing' in eleven days. POV: Ada. The beat is urgency made personal — the abstract crime acquires a countdown.

chapters.title: Cole Closes the Circle
chapters.summary: Cole burns one of Ada's aliases, forcing her rotation schedule to collapse; a cutout contact is found dead. POV: Cole. The beat is the corruption of power shown as housekeeping — murder as administrative cleanup.

chapters.title: The Trade Offer
chapters.summary: Cole contacts Ada directly: her full history and immunity in exchange for the algorithm and Elias as the fall guy. POV: Ada. The beat is temptation with teeth — the offer is genuinely survivable, which is what makes it monstrous.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: Elias discovers Ada received the offer and confronts her; Priya, tailing them, learns enough to arrest either of them. POV: Priya. The beat is triangulated betrayal — everyone is now choosing whom to sell.

chapters.title: Eleven Days, Then Nine
chapters.summary: The extraction of the flagged teenager goes wrong; Ada exposes herself to Cole's network to get the girl out. POV: Ada. The beat is sacrifice as strategy — she spends a name to buy a life.

chapters.title: The Unredacted File
chapters.summary: Priya confronts Ada with Dana Reyes's death file and the truth about the stolen identity; an uneasy alliance forms against Cole. POV: Priya. The beat is two truths meeting — the hunter becomes the witness.

chapters.title: Everything on the Table
chapters.summary: The plan: Ada will testify publicly, trading her unredacted identity — the secret worth killing for — as the price of taking Cole down. Elias insists on taking the fall instead. POV: Elias. The beat is love expressed as self-destruction refused.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Climax: at a Senate oversight session, Cole moves to have Ada discredited and detained; she walks in under her own name for the first time in six years and delivers the kill-list. POV: Ada. The beat is terror transfigured into power.

chapters.title: Interest Paid
chapters.summary: Cole's network unravels; Elias takes the charge for the server breach, and Ada watches him surrender without being able to stop it. POV: Elias. The beat is costly victory — the debt is settled, and it hurts.

chapters.title: A Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Resolution: months later, Ada — now under a name she chose herself — visits Dana Reyes's grave and then the border town where the first saved girl lives. POV: Ada. The beat is belonging finally earned: she was no one to stay safe; now she is someone by choice.
